prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S196: After normal supply is restored, transfer back is permitted only after stable conditions are confirmed and the emergency source can be unloaded safely.
S197: The Grid Interface Relay defines the operational boundary between the offshore farm and the external transmission system.
S198: Grid Interface Relay is known operationally as Wildmere.
S199: The farm exports electrical power through the Offshore Substation, Main Transformer, and export cable to the designated grid connection point.
S200: The Export Cable Monitor provides measurements that support assessment of the export path.
S201: The Grid Interface Relay exchanges authorized operating signals with the transmission system at the agreed interface.
S202: The Grid Dispatcher sets external dispatch requirements within the applicable connection agreement.
S203: The Fleet Dispatch Console allocates requested farm output among available generating units.
S204: Dispatch commands remain subject to equipment capability, protection settings, and approved operating limits.
S205: The farm reports measured active power at the grid boundary for operational monitoring and settlement processes.
S206: Reactive power capability is managed in accordance with the connection agreement and current equipment conditions.
S207: Frequency response functions are enabled only when the relevant operating mode is authorized and available.
S208: Protection coordination prevents a fault on the external system from causing unnecessary disconnection of healthy farm equipment.
S209: Loss of communications does not remove local electrical protection or equipment interlocks.
S210: A Grid Constraint may require reduced export, revised dispatch, or temporary disconnection.
S211: SCADA Gateway provides relay status and interface measurements to the farm monitoring environment.
S212: SCADA Gateway produces the Session Revocation Receipt when an authenticated control session is terminated.
S213: Maintenance Planning Engine uses the Squall Window Bulletin when reviewing the timing of planned work.
S214: Amber Quay coordinates operational notices and control-room decisions affecting the farm interface.
S215: Kestrel Bay reports its approach and departure status in accordance with the approved marine coordination procedure.
S216: The Substation Operator confirms that switching actions affecting the export path are within the authorized work scope.
S217: The Control Engineer verifies that dispatch changes are reflected in the applicable control settings before implementation.
S218: Interface alarms are prioritized according to their effect on safety, equipment protection, and continuity of export.
S219: Planned tests are coordinated to avoid conflicting with dispatch obligations or active maintenance work.
S220: A return to normal export follows confirmation that the interface is stable and all required protections are available.
S221: The Grid Interface Relay maintains the farm's dispatch boundary while allowing local systems to manage turbine-level operation.
S222: Marine coordination aligns vessel movements, personnel transfers, and shore-side support with the approved work schedule.
S223: The Marine Coordinator maintains the daily marine plan and resolves conflicts between planned activities.
S224: The Duty Planner updates work priorities when access conditions or resource availability change.
S225: The Fleet Dispatch Console uses the quality flag to support movement planning.
S226: The Vessel Master confirms departure readiness and reports any change that could affect the passage.
S227: The Crew Transfer Vessel is assigned to transfers that meet the approved operating limits.
S228: The Service Operations Vessel provides a stable offshore base when the work plan requires extended support.
S229: The Daughter Craft is used only when its task, route, and operating conditions have been reviewed.
S230: The Weather Service provides forecast information for marine planning.
S231: Copper Finch reports local sea conditions for use in access planning.
S232: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast changes and advises the Marine Coordinator when conditions may affect the plan.
S233: Weather Hold is applied when environmental limits make a planned movement or transfer unsafe.
S234: The Personnel Tracking Console maintains the offshore personnel roster and expected return times.
S235: The North Access Scanner records authorized entry at the north access point.
S236: The South Access Scanner records authorized entry at the south access point.
S237: The HSE Officer produces the Harness Audit Card before the applicable transfer activity.
S238: The Shore Control Room maintains an overview of active marine operations and operational restrictions.
S239: The Operations Radio Console supports routine communications and escalation during offshore activity.
S240: The Port Agent coordinates port services and confirms that planned departures can be supported.
S241: Mosslight records stock movements and makes current inventory information available for logistics planning.
S242: The Storekeeper prepares requested equipment for dispatch in accordance with the approved work plan.
S243: The Work Permit Portal is checked before personnel are released to perform controlled work offshore.
S244: The Rescue Coordinator maintains the response arrangements for incidents involving vessels or personnel.
S245: The Marine Coordinator records changes to the movement plan and ensures that affected teams receive the update.
S246: The Maintenance Planning Engine ranks planned and corrective work using asset condition, safety exposure, production impact, access feasibility, and resource availability.
S247: The Duty Planner reviews the ranked queue and confirms that urgent work has a clear technical basis and a feasible execution path.
